PullRequestOpener.CreateArgumentsAsync is the one place hall9k writes pull request text, and its caller already has the project. Apply the guard after the existing composition, because that composition\\u0027s bounds are measured before defusal on purpose (PullRequestBody.BoundedBlock).\\n\\nWhy it inserts a word rather than wrapping: the research in the discovery workspace\\u0027s linear-magic-word-research.md found that Linear acts on a whole phrase inside a code span or a fence, while a backtick between the word and the identifier stops it. Linear\\u0027s published matcher requires only whitespace or a colon between the two, so the guard breaks adjacency on the raw text and does not depend on whether Linear reads code. Do not reuse IsInside: skipping text already in code is the gap. The inserted word must not be issue, because linear issue is a closing phrase.\\n\\nLinear facts: the word lists move (five changes in seven months), so keep them in one place; updates is new and is on the changelog and the GitLab page rather than the GitHub page. Closing words fire on open as well as on merge, and a link can pull a Done issue back to In Progress. Negation is not read. A bare title identifier links. Unverified: whether an intervening word fully stops a link (the closest public cohorts sit at or near the rate for a bare mention), and how Linear treats identifier case.\\n\\nParked: reading attachmentsForURL after open and repairing a stray link with an Ignore line (trigger: the first observed wrong move, or a report of a parser change). A person runs the revised live check in that report before a Linear-tracked project relies on this guard; if the inserted word links, the Ignore line becomes the mechanism.\\n\\nOut of scope: commit messages. Linear acts on magic words in commits only with its commit-linking toggle on, this workspace has it off (ruling 1), and hall9k does not author them. The objective seed and the daemon\\u0027s draft objectives are unchanged for the same reason; the guard at pull request open covers them wherever they reach a pull request. Parked, with triggers, in notes/challenge-1f3e070c/journal.md: no-key branches, a non-closing word on a task\\u0027s own issue, and commit puts the Linear identifier at the front of the pull request title once, exactly as a Jira key is placed today (whole-token check, an authored title that already starts with the identifier kept as written), and a GitHub issue number still gets no prefix\u0022,\u0022The work-item line on the body renders a Linear link as [ENG-123](\\u003Cissue web URL\\u003E) with no magic word before it, so it mentions the issue without instructing Linear; when no web URL can be resolved it falls back to the existing unlinked form, Work item: linear:ENG-123\u0022,\u0022On a Linear-tracked project (one with a Linear team bound, or a task whose own reference is a Linear one), the composed pull request title and body pass through a pure Linear guard in RelayedText that works on the raw text and is deliberately not markdown-aware, so text already inside a code span or a fenced block is treated like any other text. When a linking word is directly followed on the same line by a Linear identifier other than the task\\u0027s own, a Linear issue URL with or without its slug, a markdown link to either, or a list of those, the guard inserts the neutral word ticket after the linking word, so Fixes ENG-123, DES-5, and ENG-256 becomes Fixes ticket ENG-123, DES-5, and ENG-256, and does not close ENG-2 becomes does not close ticket ENG-2. The linking words sit in one list: Linear\\u0027s closing words (close, fix, resolve, complete, and implement in every form Linear lists, plus the phrase linear issue) and its non-closing words (ref, refs, references, part of, contributes to, toward, towards, and updates); skip and ignore get the same treatment before any identifier, the task\\u0027s own included, because they unlink a pull request. The guard is idempotent, never inserts the word issue, and a test pins the objective, each criterion, the authored title and body, and the agent summary against the composed title and body, including a phrase inside a code span and one inside a fenced block\u0022,\u0022The title holds no Linear identifier but the task\\u0027s own, because a bare identifier in a title links with no magic word: the guard drops any other identifier from the title rather than rewording around it\u0022,\u0022An identifier counts only when its team key is one the install\\u0027s Linear connection can see, read across every page of teams once when the pull request text is composed, so Fix SHA-256 hashing stays as written on a Linear-tracked project. If that read fails for any reason but cancellation, the body guard falls back to matching by shape and the title rule is skipped, and opening the pull request never fails for a tracker reason\u0022,\u0022The {TEAM}-NEW form, matched in upper case against those team keys, loses its hyphen, so ENG-NEW cannot create an issue and brand-new stays as written\u0022,\u0022On a Linear-tracked project the branch slug holds no key-shaped token, matched by shape with no network read, because Linear links every identifier in a branch name; the {key} token itself is unaffected\u0022,\u0022On a project that is not Linear-tracked the title and body are byte for byte what they are today: RelayedText.WithoutClosingKeywords is unchanged, and tests pin Fix SHA-256 hashing and Fixes PROJ-1 surviving as written on a Jira-tracked and a GitHub-tracked project\u0022,\u0022The phrases relates to and related to before an identifier are left alone, because Linear documents them as changing no status, and they are how hall9k text may name another issue; a closing or non-closing word before the task\\u0027s own identifier is left alone too\u0022,\u0022Closeout posts no comment to a Linear issue and changes no Linear state: the pull request adds no Linear code to CloseoutEngine, and the close-linked-issue rule stays GitHub-only\u0022,\u0022On a Linear-tracked project, LinkedWorkItemImport finds a Linear identifier in a pull request\\u0027s title or body, bare or inside a Linear issue URL with or without its slug, only against the team keys the install\\u0027s Linear connection can see, read across every page of teams at scan time and only when the text holds a key-shaped token, so an issue from a team other than the project\\u0027s default is found and a token that merely looks like a key (UTF-8, SHA-256, CVE-2024-1) is not. A Linear identifier wins over a GitHub closing reference in the same text. A project that is not Linear-tracked makes no Linear call and behaves exactly as today. With no Linear connection, or on any failure of either Linear read other than cancellation, the scan adds no context and the adoption or review mint carries on, as an unbound Jira board or an unreadable item does today\u0022,\u0022Because hall9k relies on Linear\\u0027s branch-name linking and writes no magic word, h9k doctor warns, with no network call, when a Linear-tracked project\\u0027s branch template carries no {key} token, naming h9k project set \\u003Cproject\\u003E --branch-template \\u0022{key}-{slug}\\u0022; the default task/{shortid}-{slug} template carries no identifier for Linear to link. This covers a template changed after the bind, including --branch-template none, which the warning given at bind time does not see\u0022,\u0022Every Linear call in these tests runs against recorded responses, and no test opens a pull request or touches GitHub\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T14:24:38.881357\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"706b1c50-736d-48aa-808b-116e0f475c02","originSequence":145729,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T14:24:38.891996+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
